bands.message: Albumin is low, from poor nutrition, liver or kidney loss. Eat enough protein and see your doctor.
Albumin is normal.
Albumin is high, usually from dehydration. Drink water.
ALP is in the normal range.
ALP is raised, from liver, bone or pregnancy. Your doctor will check the cause.
ALP is high. See your doctor for liver and bone tests.
Liver enzyme ALT is normal.
ALT is mildly raised, often from fatty liver. Lose weight, avoid alcohol and recheck in 3 months.
ALT is high. Avoid alcohol and paracetamol excess; your doctor will check the cause.
ALT is very high, suggesting acute liver injury. Seek urgent review.
Amylase is normal.
Amylase is raised. Your doctor will check the pancreas. Avoid alcohol.
Amylase is high, suggesting pancreatitis. Seek urgent review for tummy pain.
Liver enzyme AST is normal.
AST is mildly raised, often from fatty liver or alcohol. Cut alcohol and recheck.
AST is high. Avoid alcohol; your doctor will check the liver and heart.
AST is very high. Seek urgent review.
Bicarbonate is low, so the blood is more acidic. Common in kidney disease; your doctor will review.
Bicarbonate is normal.
Bicarbonate is high, often with vomiting or water tablets. Your doctor will review.
Sugar under 3.9 is low. Take a sweet drink, then eat. Tell your doctor if it happens often.
Sugar 3.9-7.8 is normal.
Sugar 7.8-11 is raised. A fasting test or HbA1c will clarify.
Sugar over 11 is high. See your doctor to review treatment.
Sugar over 14 is very high. Seek urgent help if vomiting, drowsy or breathing fast.
Urea is in the normal range.
Urea is raised, often from dehydration or kidney strain. Drink well and recheck.
Urea is high. See your doctor to check kidney function.
Calcium is very low and can cause spasms. Seek urgent review.
Calcium is low. Milk, yoghurt, small fish and green leaves help; supplements may be needed.
Calcium is normal.
Calcium is high. Drink plenty of water; your doctor will check the cause.
Calcium is very high. Seek urgent medical review.
Calcium is low. Milk, yoghurt, small fish and green leaves help; supplements may be needed.
Calcium is normal.
Calcium is high. Drink plenty of water; your doctor will check the cause.
Chloride is low, often with vomiting or water tablets. Your doctor will review.
Chloride is normal.
Chloride is high, usually with dehydration. Drink water and recheck.
Muscle enzyme CK is normal.
CK is raised, from exercise, injury or statin side effect. Tell your doctor about muscle pain.
CK is high. Stop your statin and see your doctor today if you have muscle pain or dark urine.
Kidney clearance is reduced. Some medicine doses may need adjusting; avoid ibuprofen painkillers.
Kidney clearance is normal.
CRP (inflammation marker) is normal.
CRP is raised, showing some infection or inflammation.
CRP is high, suggesting significant infection. See your doctor if unwell or feverish.
Your 10-year heart risk is low. Keep active, avoid tobacco and recheck in 5 years.
Your 10-year heart risk is moderate. Control pressure, sugar and cholesterol; stop smoking.
Your 10-year heart risk is high. A statin and blood pressure control are strongly advised.
Your heart risk is very high. Take statin and pressure tablets daily and stop smoking now.
Your ECG (heart tracing) is normal.
Your ECG shows a change that your doctor will explain and follow up.
Kidney function is very low (stage 5). Your kidney team will guide dialysis or other care.
Kidney function is severely reduced (stage 4). Follow diet advice; avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers.
Kidney function is moderately reduced (stage 3). Control pressure and sugar; recheck 6-monthly.
Kidney function is mildly reduced. Keep pressure under 130/80 and avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers.
Kidney function is normal. Good pressure and sugar control keep it that way.
ESR (inflammation marker) is normal.
ESR is raised, showing inflammation or infection somewhere. Your doctor will look for the cause.
Fasting sugar under 55 is dangerously low. Take sugar now and tell your doctor to review medicines.
Fasting sugar under 70 is low. Eat regularly and tell your doctor if you take insulin or gliclazide.
Fasting sugar 70-99 is normal. Keep up healthy eating and activity.
Fasting sugar 100-125 is borderline. Cut sugar and rice portions, walk daily, recheck in 3 months.
Fasting sugar 126 or more is high. Take medicines regularly and discuss control with your doctor.
Fasting sugar over 250 is very high. See your doctor soon; seek urgent help if vomiting or drowsy.
Ferritin is low, meaning iron stores are empty. Iron tablets for 3 months and iron-rich foods help.
Iron stores are normal.
Ferritin is high, from inflammation, liver disease or iron overload. Your doctor will review.
Kidney function is very low (stage 5). Your kidney team will guide dialysis or other care.
Kidney function is severely reduced (stage 4). Follow diet advice; avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers.
Kidney function is moderately reduced (stage 3). Control pressure and sugar; recheck 6-monthly.
Kidney function is mildly reduced. Keep pressure under 130/80 and avoid ibuprofen-type painkillers.
Kidney function is normal. Good pressure and sugar control keep it that way.

sourceNames: Glucose, serum 2 hrs post 75g oral glucose (mg/dL)

bands.message: Your 2-hour sugar is under 140: normal. Stay active and recheck as advised.
A 2-hour sugar of 140-199 means prediabetes. Weight loss and walking can prevent diabetes.
A 2-hour sugar of 200 or more is in the diabetes range. See your doctor to confirm and plan.
Your personal sugar target is set with your doctor. Aim for it steadily; small changes count.
Haematocrit is low, consistent with anaemia. Iron-rich food and finding the cause help.
Haematocrit is normal.
Haematocrit is high, often from dehydration or smoking. Your doctor will review.
Haemoglobin is very low. Seek urgent review; you may need a transfusion.
Haemoglobin under 13 means anaemia. Iron-rich food and iron tablets help; find the cause.
Haemoglobin is normal.
Haemoglobin is high, often from smoking or dehydration. Your doctor will review.
Haemoglobin is very low. Seek urgent review; you may need a transfusion.
Haemoglobin under 12 means anaemia. Iron-rich food and iron tablets help; find the cause.
Haemoglobin is normal.
Haemoglobin is high, often from smoking or dehydration. Your doctor will review.
HbA1c under 6.5%: excellent control. If you get low sugars, tell your doctor - dose may be too high.
HbA1c 6.5-7.5%: reasonable control. Keep taking medicines, watch portions and stay active.
HbA1c over 7.5% is high. Lowering it protects kidneys, eyes and heart. Ask your doctor to review it.
HbA1c over 9%: sugar is far too high. See your doctor soon to adjust treatment. Never miss doses.
HbA1c 6.5-7.5% is reasonable, but at your age aiming lower gives decades of protection. Keep going.
To lower HbA1c: every dose, smaller rice portions, no sugary drinks, daily walk. Recheck in 3 months
HbA1c under 5.7% is normal. Stay active; recheck in 1-3 years, sooner if diabetes is in the family.
HbA1c 5.7-6.4% means prediabetes. Losing 5% of weight and daily walking can prevent diabetes.
HbA1c 6.5% or more is in the diabetes range. See your doctor to confirm and plan treatment.
HDL (good cholesterol) is low. Exercise, stopping smoking and weight loss raise it.
HDL (good cholesterol) is in the normal range.
HDL (good cholesterol) is high, which protects your heart. Well done.
Active calcium is low. Your doctor will review vitamin D and other causes.
Active calcium is normal.
Active calcium is high. Drink water and see your doctor to find the cause.
LDL (bad cholesterol) under 2.6 is optimal. Keep taking any statin prescribed.
LDL 2.6-3.3 is acceptable for most; with diabetes or heart disease, aim under 2.6.
LDL 3.4-4.9 is raised. Diet changes and possibly a statin will lower it.
LDL over 4.9 is very high. See your doctor - a statin is usually needed.
Lymphocytes are low, often after viral illness or steroids.
Lymphocytes are normal.
Lymphocytes are raised, often from viral infection. Your doctor will review if persistent.
Lymphocyte percentage is low. Your doctor will interpret with the full count.
Lymphocyte percentage is normal.
Lymphocyte percentage is raised, often from viral infection.
Magnesium is low, often from stomach tablets or water tablets. Green leaves, nuts and seeds help.
Magnesium is normal.
Magnesium is high. Your doctor will review kidney function and supplements.
Red cells carry less haemoglobin than normal, suggesting iron deficiency.
MCH is normal.
MCH is high, often with low B12 or folate.
MCHC is low, suggesting iron deficiency.
MCHC is normal.
MCHC is high. Your doctor will review.
Red cells are small, usually from iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait. Iron studies will clarify.
Red cell size is normal.
Red cells are large, often from low B12 or folate, or alcohol. Your doctor will check.
Neutrophils are low, raising infection risk. Report fever promptly.
Neutrophils are normal.
Neutrophils are raised, usually from bacterial infection or stress.
Neutrophil percentage is low. Your doctor will interpret with the full count.
Neutrophil percentage is normal.
Neutrophil percentage is raised, usually from infection.
You have never smoked - one of the best things for your heart and lungs. Keep it that way.
Phosphate is low. Your doctor will review diet and vitamin D.
Phosphate is normal.
Phosphate is high, common in kidney disease. Limit processed food and colas; take binders if given.
Platelets are very low, raising bleeding risk. Seek urgent review; avoid aspirin and ibuprofen.
Platelets are low. Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen unless told otherwise; report any bleeding.
Platelet count is normal.
Platelets are raised, often from infection or iron deficiency. Your doctor will recheck.
Sugar after a meal under 70 is low. Eat regularly and tell your doctor if on insulin or gliclazide.
Sugar after a meal under 140 is normal. Well done.
Sugar 140-199 after a meal is raised. Smaller portions and a walk after eating help.
Sugar over 200 after meals is high. Review your diet and medicines with your doctor.
Sugar over 250 after meals is very high. See your doctor soon; urgent help if vomiting or drowsy.
Potassium is dangerously low. Seek urgent medical review.
Potassium is low, often from water tablets or diarrhoea. Eat bananas and coconut water; recheck.
Potassium is normal.
Potassium is high. Your doctor will review kidney tablets and diet. Limit bananas and coconut water.
Potassium is dangerously high and can affect the heart. Seek urgent medical review.
Sugar under 50 is dangerously low. Take sugar now and seek help if not better in 15 minutes.
Sugar under 70 is low. Take a sweet drink, then eat. Tell your doctor if it happens often.
Random sugar under 140 is normal.
Random sugar 140-199 is raised. A fasting test or HbA1c will clarify.
Random sugar over 200 is high. See your doctor to review treatment.
Sugar over 400 is dangerously high. Seek urgent help, especially if vomiting or drowsy.
Red cell count is low, consistent with anaemia.
Red cell count is normal.
Red cell count is high. Your doctor will review.
Creatinine is low, usually from low muscle mass. Not a concern on its own.
Creatinine is normal, so your kidneys are filtering well.
Creatinine is raised, so kidneys are under strain. Drink well, avoid ibuprofen and see your doctor.
Creatinine is high. Your doctor needs to review kidney function and medicines soon.
Creatinine is very high. Seek medical review urgently.
Creatinine is low, usually from low muscle mass. Not a concern on its own.
Creatinine is normal, so your kidneys are filtering well.
Creatinine is raised, so kidneys are under strain. Drink well, avoid ibuprofen and see your doctor.
Creatinine is high. Your doctor needs to review kidney function and medicines soon.
Serum iron is low. Eat greens, lentils, meat and eggs; take iron tablets if prescribed.
Serum iron is normal.
Serum iron is high. Your doctor will review.
Sodium is dangerously low. Seek urgent medical review.
Sodium is low, often from water tablets or excess fluid. Your doctor will review medicines.
Sodium is normal.
Sodium is high, usually from dehydration. Drink water and recheck.
Sodium is dangerously high. Seek urgent medical review.
Bilirubin is normal.
Bilirubin is mildly raised. Often harmless (Gilbert's) but your doctor will check the liver.
Bilirubin is high and may cause yellow eyes. See your doctor soon.

sourceNames: Serum or plasma total cholesterol measurement (mg/dL)

bands.message: Total cholesterol under 5.2 is in the healthy range. Keep up the good diet and activity.
Cholesterol 5.2-6.2 is borderline. Less coconut oil and fried food, more vegetables and walking.
Cholesterol over 6.2 is high. A statin may be advised, especially with diabetes or heart risk.
Cholesterol over 7.8 is very high. See your doctor - treatment is needed to protect your heart.
Total cholesterol under 200 is in the healthy range. Keep up the good diet and activity.
Cholesterol 200-239 is borderline. Less coconut oil and fried food, more vegetables and walking.
Cholesterol over 240 is high. A statin may be advised, especially with diabetes or heart risk.
Cholesterol over 300 is very high. See your doctor - treatment is needed to protect your heart.
Total blood fats are in the normal range.
Total blood fats are raised. A full cholesterol profile will guide treatment.
Total protein is low. Your doctor will check nutrition, liver and kidneys.
Total protein is normal.
Total protein is high. Your doctor will review the cause.
Triglycerides under 1.7 are normal.
Triglycerides are borderline. Cut sugar, alcohol and fried food, and walk daily.
Triglycerides are high. Reduce sugar, alcohol and oil; good sugar control also lowers them.
Triglycerides are very high, with a risk of pancreatitis. See your doctor soon.
Troponin is normal - no sign of heart muscle damage.
Troponin is raised, suggesting heart muscle strain or damage. This needs urgent hospital review.
Troponin is normal - no sign of heart muscle damage.
Troponin is raised, suggesting heart muscle strain or damage. This needs urgent hospital review.
TSH is low, suggesting an overactive thyroid. Your doctor will check thyroid hormone levels.
Thyroid function (TSH) is normal.
TSH is high, suggesting an underactive thyroid. Levothyroxine may be needed or the dose increased.
Urea is low. Usually not a concern; can reflect low protein intake.
Urea is in the normal range.
Urea is raised, often from dehydration or kidney strain. Drink well and recheck.
Urea is high. See your doctor to check kidney function.
Uric acid is normal.
Uric acid is high, raising gout and stone risk. Cut alcohol, red meat and sugary drinks; drink water
No significant protein in urine. Good news.
Protein in urine is an early kidney warning. Control sugar and pressure and recheck in 3 months.
No significant protein leak from the kidneys. Good news.
A small protein leak is an early kidney warning. ACE/ARB tablets and good sugar and BP control help.
A large protein leak means kidney damage. See your doctor to strengthen kidney protection.
No sugar in your urine. Good sign.
Sugar in urine usually means blood sugar is high. A blood test will confirm.
VLDL is in the normal range.
VLDL is raised, usually with high triglycerides. Cut sugar, alcohol and fried food.
White cells are very low, raising infection risk. Seek urgent review for any fever.
White cells are low. Your doctor will review; report any fever promptly.
White cell count is normal.
White cells are raised, usually from infection or inflammation.
White cells are very high. Seek prompt medical review.
